article_notes: Onderstepoort (OVAH) pooled cohort of 320 B. rossi mono-infections (PCR/RLB), 2006-2016, from three prospective databases that have been published elsewhere (Schoeman, Goddard, Leisewitz studies, Koster 2015 etc.), so dogs overlap with many other Onderstepoort articles. All samples taken before treatment. Two severity groupings: died vs survived (34 vs 286; euthanasia counted with death; to discharge) and collapsed vs able to stand (72 vs 248). Most group comparisons are text statements without values or p values; the per-group table is Table S1 (not in text). Multivariable logistic regression identified no independent predictors and no model was reported. Joint correspondence analysis (Figure 2) is graphical. Several inconsistencies between text and tables are recorded in row notes (band OR 4.9 vs 5.9; urea OR 9.1 vs 30.95; bilirubin Se/Sp). Group sizes per variable are mostly not printed.

severity_definitions.label: died vs survived
severity_definitions.definition: Short-term outcome: survival to discharge vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis. 34/320 died; all treated dogs that died did so within 24 h of admission.
severity_definitions.quote: Outcome was recorded as short-term survival (i.e. until discharge), or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis.

severity_definitions.label: collapsed vs non-collapsed at presentation
severity_definitions.definition: Collapse at presentation = unable to stand unaided (72/320). Used by the authors as a severity grouping for many laboratory comparisons.
severity_definitions.quote: Seventy-two of the 320 cases (22.5%) were collapsed at presentation (unable to stand unaided).
